source_review_summary: Mechanism evidence was elevated from automated keyword notes to source-reviewed direct/functional classes with section, figure, table, method, and supplement-caption locators.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The mutant peptides directly perturb bacterial-model membranes, with source-reviewed support from membrane depolarization, NPN outer-membrane permeability, and calcein leakage assays; MC1-2 is generally the strongest in these assays.
direct_assay_types: calcein leakage from PG/CL and PG/CL/PE liposomes
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure-only curve values beyond the article text were not OCR-normalized; qualitative/direct-assay class is supported.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides bind LPS and alter LPS aggregate state, supported by ITC thermodynamic parameters, DLS LPS micelle dissociation, and LPS-induced peptide conformation evidence.
direct_assay_types: dynamic light scattering of LPS micelles

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper reports functional anti-inflammatory effects: mutant peptides inhibit LPS-induced TNF-α and IL-6 release in RAW264.7 cells, and MC1-1 reduces serum cytokines and improves survival in the LPS-challenged mouse model.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: MC1-1, MC1-2, and MC1-3 in vitro; MC1-1 in vivo
